items.title: The inverse system of powers of an ideal is pro-isomorphic to the system of Koszul complexes
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors

items.difficulty_reason: The statement says that in the Koszul setup of the section, over a Noetherian ring, the inverse system of powers of the ideal is pro-isomorphic to the inverse system of Koszul complexes, as objects of the derived category (statement lines 29647-29652, formulated inside the situation of the section). The proof replaces the powers by the system generated by the powers of the chosen generators, forms the inverse system of distinguished triangles with the cone of the comparison, and reduces to pro-zero-ness of the cones: the cones are bounded because the Koszul complex sits between degrees minus r plus one and zero, their cohomology vanishes in nonnegative degrees and agrees with the Koszul cohomology below, and the pro-zero property of the latter was established earlier, which is where the Noetherian hypothesis is used (proof lines 29654-29673). The reduction to a statement about cones is what makes the argument short. The counted statement depends on the situation of the section, which is delivered as the context span, and refers three times to earlier results, which are carried as navigation stubs.
